- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c21945d227b2a5e680af14635865f891108e10a8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

Head-sha: 77dbe40f6e18a56616c6a325c2b30288f6454cb0

I ran `check-governed-merges --branch` at this head. It reads tier H: one path is under `skills/**`, and 124 changed lines is under the 3000-line threshold. The low-risk skills arm reads NOT MEASURED, and it cannot apply here, because six of the seven paths are off the arm's allowlist. Landing goes to the seat's at-tier review and then to the governed approver. This verdict does not ready the PR.

#### Must-fix
None.

#### Should-fix
None.

#### What I checked
- **Shape and scope.**
  - `Fixes #34839` is present. Clause-② `no` and Metadata-protocol `none` match claim 6964781167.
  - All seven files are on the claim's file surface. The ratchet script is untouched, as the claim allows when the edit pays for itself.
  - Both commits are text only, plus the test edit the card asks for in item 6.
- **The served block, read from the runtime at this head.**
  - `approval-service.ts#attachViewers` sets four leaves.
  - `can_override_approve` is computed as `canOverride && !overrideApprovesOwnRequest(row, person)`. So the server never serves it `true` beside a `false` `can_override`, as the new `approvalOverride.ts` text says.
  - The predicates in `sys-approval-request.object.ts` match the text in all four places:
    - `approval_approve` ORs in `can_override_approve`.
    - `approval_reject`, `approval_reassign` and `approval_recall` OR in `can_override`.
    - `send_back` and `request_info` read `can_act` alone.
    - `remind` and `resubmit` read `is_submitter` alone.
    - `comment` reads `can_act` or a pending `is_submitter`.
  - So the new `account.app.ts` sentence, "every one is gated on a leaf of the served `record.viewer` block", is true. The old sentence, "all eight … `can_act || can_override`", was false.
- **`approvalOverride.ts`.** `actionAdmittedByOverride` is `predicateSource(visible).includes('can_override')`. That substring catches both leaf names, as the docblock now says. No code line changed.
- **Checklist (item 4).**
  - Three items each carry a revision bump and a dated history entry, ref #34839.
  - `approvals.record-page-decisions` steps[9] and acceptance[4]: the item's admin submitted the request. Earlier steps say this already ("Reply … the admin holds it as the submitter"), and so does revision 5. So off the slate the admin reads `can_override_approve` false, and the `approval_approve` predicate hides Approve. Dropping "Override Approve" from the folded menu follows from source. The PR body and the dev report both say this was not re-run in a browser, and both name the run it is owed.
  - I grepped the tree at this head for text the PR could leave false.
    - `approvals.inbox-metadata-actions` acceptance[1] still names "Override Approve". That is correct: it is the dev admin on another submitter's request, where `can_override_approve` is true.
    - `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx:945-967` already names all four leaves.
    - The other hits are history entries and CHANGELOGs, which stay as they were.
- **The skill row (item 5).** `openNodeRequest`'s `admin_rescue` branch opens the request on `organizationAdministrators`, which are the TENANT_ADMIN rung holders of the request's organization. "Opens on the organization's administrators" is accurate. The file goes from 23661 to 23652 bytes, the dev measured 5913 tokens against a 5916 ceiling, and the row is unchanged.
- **Item 6.** Both describe blocks rebuild the double in `beforeEach` (`makeFakeEngine()`, lines 106 and 242). The body's note that the `finally` fixes no observed leak is correct. The restore is harmless.
- **Item 7.** The `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` job builds and runs `@objectstack/driver-sql` only. With no lane that runs `ApprovalService` on a case-folding store, no pin is correct, and it is reported rather than invented.
- **Changeset.**
  - It covers `@objectstack/skills` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` at patch, the right level for Metadata-protocol `none`.
  - The `spec` docblock sits on a non-exported const. The dev measured that it does not reach `dist`, which I did not re-run.
  - `@object-ui/app-shell` is `"private": true`. `plugin-approvals` moved only a test file.
- **Tests.** The body gives real commands with counts: 1741 of 1741 in plugin-approvals, the audit file at 20/20 both before and after, typecheck, and `check:generated`. It names the two NOT MEASURED families and the one ui `scripts/` failure with its cause, and it does not round them up to a pass.
- **CI on this head, read at review time.** Nothing is red.
  - Concluded green: PR-body guards, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, and the plan jobs.
  - Still running: Test Core 1-10, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, and the remaining Lint and Type Check families.
  - Landing waits for these to go green.

#### Notes (nit-level, may stay open)
- **N1.** In `approvalOverride.ts:38-39`, the quoted shape `… can_act == true || … can_override == true` is said to be what "Reject, Reassign and Recall read". Recall's first arm is the pending-or-returned `is_submitter` term, not `can_act`, so the quote fits Reject and Reassign only. The test reads only the `can_override` substring, so the conclusion stands.
- **N2.** The skill row leaves out the rescue path's own fallback. With no organization, or when the administrators read fails, the request opens on the slate that names no one, and only the override acts on it (`organizationAdministrators` docblock). That is fine for a one-line table row. `approvals.mdx` carries the detail.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `77dbe40f6e18a56616c6a325c2b30288f6454cb0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md + packages/platform-objects/src/apps/account.app.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/approvalOverride.ts, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/approvals.json, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-override-audit.test.ts
Security-touching: yes

Inputs read: card #34839 body and its three comments (triage 6949955415, claim 6964781167, os-dev-report 6966130282); PR #35066 body, its seven-file list, the net diff `origin/main...77dbe40f6e` (merge base `367e324eeb`, 84 insertions, 40 deletions); the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read at the head, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: no change. No schema line, no `.describe()` string, no predicate and no runtime statement moves. The `object.zod.ts` hunk is the jsdoc over the non-exported `ATTACHED_ON_READ_NAME` / attachedOnRead schema const (:2879-2890). Right.
- Generated surface: nothing owed. No `.describe()` moved, and no file under `content/docs/references/` or the spec's generated output carries the edited sentence (searched at the head). `Spec property liveness` is success on the head. Right.
- Public surface: one published sentence changes, the `onEmptyApprovers` row of the automation skill (:375). The comment in `account.app.ts` ships in `@objectstack/platform-objects` build output as text only. `@object-ui/app-shell` is private. Right.
- Checklist: three items re-pointed, each with a revision bump and a dated history entry (`inbox-metadata-actions` 9 to 10, `viewer-gating-submitter-side` 7 to 8, `record-page-decisions` 8 to 9). One of them changes an expected outcome (see ④); the other two only name the leaves. Right.
- Test file: one case restructured, assertions unchanged (see ④). Right.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/34839-approvals-viewer-block-descriptions.md`: patch for `@objectstack/skills` and `@objectstack/platform-objects`. Patch matches what publishes: a corrected skill sentence and a comment. `@objectstack/spec` is not named, which is right for a jsdoc on a non-exported const with no generated artifact moved. `Check Changeset` is success on the head.

Clause-②: no — the PR body and the changeset both carry it, and it holds: nothing a consumer could author or call is narrowed, widened or re-typed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the os-dev-report. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, card item 6 premise partly false: confirmed. Both describe blocks rebuild the double in `beforeEach` (`approval-override-audit.test.ts` :106-107, :242-243), so the replaced `find` could not leak. The `finally` is harmless and is what the card asked for.
- Dev flag, card item 7 no pin added: accepted as reported. The card conditions the pin on a case-folding lane that runs this service; the dev reports none does. Not verified beyond the card and PR text; it stays an out-of-scope note, not a finding on this diff.
- Dev flag, `record-page-decisions` expectation read from source and not run in a browser: answered in ④, true by code. The browser run stays owed the next time the item is executed, as the history entry itself says.
- Dev flag, PR-body HTML comment rule conflict: process question for the seat, outside this record.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Check-runs on the head when this record was written: 23 success, 10 skipped, 34 in progress, none failed or cancelled. Completed green includes `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Check Documentation Links`, `PR-body guards`. Still running: every `Test Core` and `Test UI` shard, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`. This verdict is the design judgment; it does not stand in for those gates, and the seat reads their conclusions before it lands anything.

### ④ Design judgment

Read against the head tree. `S` = `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`, `O` = `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts`.

The facts every changed sentence rests on:

- Four leaves served: `attachViewers` sets `can_act`, `is_submitter`, `can_override`, `can_override_approve` (S:10888-10893). The object declares the same four under `attachedOnRead` (O:543).
- `can_override_approve` is `canOverride && !overrideApprovesOwnRequest(row, person)` (S:10892); `overrideApprovesOwnRequest` is the submitter test over the context's recorded actor (S:1270-1272). So it is never true beside a false `can_override`.
- The submitter exclusion at the door: `decideNode` refuses `decision === 'approve' && viaOverride && overrideApprovesOwnRequest(raw, decider)` with FORBIDDEN (S:5754-5759), the same predicate as the flag.
- Predicates: `approval_approve` ORs in `can_override_approve` (O:659-661); `approval_reject` (O:705-707), `approval_reassign` (O:734-736) and `approval_recall` (O:853-856) OR in `can_override`; `approval_send_back` and `approval_request_info` read `can_act` alone (O:765, O:786); `approval_remind` and `approval_resubmit` read `is_submitter` (O:813, O:880); `approval_comment` reads `can_act` or `is_submitter` (O:933-936). All nine gate on a leaf of `record.viewer`.

`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (hits). The docblock names the four leaves and says predicates gate on `can_act` for an approver's actions, `is_submitter` for the submitter's, and an override arm reading `can_override_approve` on Approve and `can_override` on Reject, Reassign and Recall. Each clause is true against the lines above. It implements the maintainer ruling of 2026-11-17 (option B) as the first consumer, plugin-approvals, carries it. Holds.

`skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md` (hits). `admin_rescue` now reads "request opens on the organization's administrators; never waves through, never kills the run". True: the empty-slate branch resolves `organizationAdministrators(requestOrg)` and adopts them as the slate, as ordinary `user` approvers in the ordinary inbox (S:5176-5240; resolver at S:4275, tenant-admin rung of the request's organization, platform administrators not added). The removed text ("only a privileged admin can act via Reassign") was false after #22824. The new wording matches `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` :118-119, :304-305 and :341-342, which is what the card told it to align with. An authoring agent following the row now tells the user the right thing, which is the card's acceptance scenario. The rest of the row is unchanged, and the neighbouring `excludeSubmitter` row stays consistent with it. Holds.

`packages/platform-objects/src/apps/account.app.ts` (implementing). "Every one is gated on a leaf of the served `record.viewer` block" is true for all nine declared actions. The old text ("all eight ... `can_act || can_override`") was wrong on both the count and the gate. The override-arm clause matches O. Holds.

`ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/approvalOverride.ts` (implementing). Comment only, no code line moved. Module docblock: two override leaves, which action reads which, the second never true beside a false first, and "the test is a substring match on `can_override`, which both leaf names carry" — the code is `predicateSource(...).includes('can_override')` (:122-125), so it is exact. `ViewerBlockLike` docblock: the interface declares three leaves and the module reads the fourth only through Approve's predicate text; true, no code reads `viewer.can_override_approve`. `actionAdmittedByOverride` docblock: true. Tried to break it: an override-only viewer who submitted the request has `can_override` true and `can_override_approve` false; `isOverrideOnlyViewer` is true and Approve matches the substring, but Approve's own `visible` is false, so it is never drawn and never mislabelled. Holds.

`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/approvals.json` (implementing). The two leaf-naming items are true against O and S. The re-pointed expectation in `approvals.record-page-decisions` steps[9] and acceptance[4]: the item's admin is the request's submitter (the unchanged text has the admin hold Reply and Recall as the submitter). Off the slate that viewer is served `can_act` false, `can_override` true, `can_override_approve` false (S:10888-10893). `DeclaredActionsBar` folds the levers that `actionAdmittedByOverride` matches for an override-only viewer (:965-966) and each folded lever keeps its own `visible` verdict (:141-147, :228-232), so Approve, whose override arm reads the false leaf, is absent; Override Reject, Override Reassign and the plain Recall remain. The new expectation is true by code, and the old one ("lists Override Approve") would now fail against a correct build. The server refuses the forged call too (S:5754-5759). Source[4] reads `can_override_approve` correctly. Holds; the history entries say plainly it was not re-run.

`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-override-audit.test.ts` (implementing). The case keeps the double's own `find` reference, runs the same four assertions with the same regexes and the same expected slates inside `try`, and puts the reference back in `finally`. No assertion is removed, loosened or made conditional; a failing `expect` still throws through the `finally`. Not a weakening. Holds.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits:

- N1 (nit) — the skill row no longer says what happens when the organization has no administrator to open on (no organization, or the only administrator is the submitter): the request then keeps the slate that names no one and only the administrator override moves it (S:4268-4272, S:5199-5220; docs section "When a slate names no one", approvals.mdx :547 onward). The card ruled the wording to match the docs' one-line form, and the file sits 3 tokens under its ratchet ceiling, so this is a follow-up at most, not a defect of this change.
- N2 (nit) — `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/account-approvals-nav.test.ts` :10 still carries the old `can_act || can_override` comment that this PR corrected in `account.app.ts`. Outside the diff and outside the card's list; a follow-up, not owed here.

Security-touching is `yes` and meant: the skill hunk teaches who may decide an approval request with an empty slate, and the other hunks describe the administrator override and the rule that it never approves its actor's own request. The seat adopting this record adds the `security` label.
